source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: The ethical principle that requires researchers to protect participants from physical and psychological harm is:
questions.rationale: Beneficence means doing good and protecting participants from harm and exploitation.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 5 Summary (PDF p. 148)
questions.quote: Beneficence involves the performance of some good and the protection of participants from physical and psychological harm and exploitation.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A mother tells the researcher she wants to stop answering the questionnaire halfway. The researcher lets her withdraw without penalty. This respects her right to:
questions.rationale: Respect for human dignity includes self-determination: voluntary participation and the right to withdraw.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 5 Summary (PDF p. 148)
questions.quote: Respect for human dignity involves the participants’ right to self-determination, which includes participants’ right to participate in a study voluntarily.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Participants are selected fairly and not because they are poor or easy to recruit. This applies the principle of:
questions.rationale: Justice includes the right to fair treatment (fair selection and treatment) and the right to privacy.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 5 Summary (PDF p. 148)
questions.quote: Justice includes the right to fair treatment and the right to privacy.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Before enrolling participants, the researcher explains the study's purpose, risks, benefits and their rights. This is:
questions.rationale: Full disclosure fully describes the study, rights, costs and benefits so participants can give informed consent.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 5 Summary (PDF p. 148)
questions.quote: Full disclosure means that researchers have fully described to prospective participants their rights and the costs and benefits of the study.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Questionnaires are returned without names or codes, so even the researcher cannot tell who answered. This protects privacy through:
questions.rationale: Anonymity means not even the researcher knows identities; confidentiality means identities are known but protected.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 5 Summary (PDF p. 149)
questions.quote: Privacy can be maintained through anonymity (wherein not even researchers know participants’ identities)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A researcher interviews patients by name but stores data under code numbers and never reports names. This protects:
questions.rationale: Confidentiality procedures safeguard data when the researcher knows participants' identities.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 5 Summary (PDF p. 149)
questions.quote: or through formal confidentiality procedures that safeguard the participants’ data.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Before starting a study, the researcher weighs the possible benefits to participants and society against the costs to individuals. This is a:
questions.rationale: A risk/benefit assessment is a key procedure for safeguarding participants' rights.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 5 Summary (PDF p. 148)
questions.quote: In a risk/benefit assessment, the potential benefits of the study to individual participants and to society are weighed against the costs to individuals.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: After data collection, the researcher meets participants to explain the study further and hear their concerns. This is called:
questions.rationale: Debriefing gives participants more information and a chance to air complaints after data collection.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 5 Summary (PDF p. 149)
questions.quote: Researchers sometimes offer debriefing sessions after data collection to provide participants with more information or an opportunity to air complaints.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which group needs additional protection as research participants because they cannot make a fully informed decision?
questions.rationale: Vulnerable groups include children, people with diminished autonomy (e.g., prisoners) and those at heightened risk (pregnant women, the terminally ill).
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 5 Summary (PDF p. 149)
questions.quote: Vulnerable groups require additional protection.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Before data collection, a nursing study should be reviewed by a(n):
questions.rationale: External ethics review of studies with human participants is expected; in the Philippines, ethics review is done by accredited research ethics committees.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 5 Summary (PDF p. 149)
questions.quote: External review of the ethical aspects of a study by a human subjects committee

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: The statement that describes the nature, background, significance and knowledge gaps of the issue to be studied is the:
questions.rationale: The problem statement articulates the nature, context and significance of the research problem.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 6 Summary (PDF p. 168)
questions.quote: The problem statement articulates the nature, context, and significance of a problem to be studied.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: "Mothers who receive home visits will have higher immunization completion rates than mothers who do not." This is a:
questions.rationale: It predicts a relationship and its direction (higher).
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 6 Summary (PDF p. 168)
questions.quote: Directional hypotheses predict the direction of a relationship; nondirectional hypotheses predict the existence of relationships, not their direction.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: "There is no difference in the anxiety scores of patients who did and did not receive preoperative teaching." This is a:
questions.rationale: The null hypothesis states no relationship and is the hypothesis tested statistically.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 6 Summary (PDF p. 168)
questions.quote: null hypotheses, which express the absence of a relationship, are the hypotheses subjected to statistical testing.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A student writes, "The results proved our hypothesis." The instructor corrects her because hypotheses are:
questions.rationale: Hypotheses are never proved or disproved; data support or fail to support them.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 6 Summary (PDF p. 168)
questions.quote: Hypotheses are never proved or disproved—they are accepted or rejected, supported or not supported by the data.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A hypothesis must state the expected relationship between:
questions.rationale: A hypothesis predicts the relationship between independent and dependent variables.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 6 Summary (PDF p. 168)
questions.quote: A hypothesis states predicted relationships between two or more variables

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which is a primary source for a literature review?
options: The original study report by its researchers
A textbook summary of the study
questions.rationale: A primary source is the original report by the researcher; reviews should rely mostly on primary sources.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 7 Summary (PDF p. 188)
questions.quote: A primary source is the original description of a study prepared by the researcher who conducted it

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A nurse finds more studies by checking the reference lists of a key article. This search strategy is the:
questions.rationale: Ancestry tracks earlier studies cited in a report; descendancy finds later studies that cited a pivotal study.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 7 Summary (PDF p. 188)
questions.quote: the ancestry approach (tracking down earlier studies cited in a reference list of a report)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: The main purpose of the review of related literature is to show:
options: What is known and what gaps exist
questions.rationale: The review points out what has been studied, how dependable the studies are and what gaps remain.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 7 Summary (PDF p. 188)
questions.quote: The reviewers’ role is to point out what has been studied, how adequate and dependable the studies are, and what gaps exist in the body of research.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A theory that addresses a specific phenomenon, such as pain or uncertainty in illness, is a:
questions.rationale: Grand theories describe large segments of human experience; middle-range theories focus on specific phenomena.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 8 Summary (PDF p. 206)
questions.quote: Grand theories (or macrotheories) attempt to describe large segments of the human experience. Middle-range theories are specific to certain phenomena.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: The four central concepts of nursing models (the metaparadigm) are person, environment, health and:
questions.rationale: Models of nursing center on human beings, environment, health and nursing.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 8 Summary (PDF p. 206)
questions.quote: The concepts central to models of nursing are human beings, environment, health, and nursing.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A nurse researcher uses Bandura's Social Cognitive Theory, which came from psychology. This is called a:
questions.rationale: Non-nursing theories used in nursing research are borrowed; once confirmed useful, they become shared theories.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 8 Summary (PDF p. 206)
questions.quote: Nonnursing models used by nurse researchers (e.g., Bandura’s Social Cognitive Theory) are referred to as borrowed theories

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which nursing model is cited as an example used in nursing research?
questions.rationale: Roy's Adaptation Model is a model of nursing; the others come from other disciplines.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 8 Summary (PDF p. 206)
questions.quote: An example of a model of nursing used by nurse researchers is Roy’s Adaptation Model.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: The overall conceptual underpinning of a study, including its rationale and conceptual definitions, is the:
questions.rationale: A framework provides the conceptual basis of a study.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 8 Summary (PDF p. 206)
questions.quote: A framework is the conceptual underpinning of a study, including an overall rationale and conceptual definitions of key concepts.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Qualitative researchers who build a theory from their data use which type of reasoning?
questions.rationale: Grounded theories are data-driven explanations developed through inductive processes; testing hypotheses from theory is deductive.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 8 Summary (PDF p. 206)
questions.quote: Some qualitative researchers seek to develop grounded theories, data-driven explanations to account for phenomena under study through inductive processes.
